bibliography.title: Rapid Poison: Practical Poisoning Attacks Against the Rapid Response Framework

sections.title: F. Mechanistic Analysis of the Omission Attack
H. Verifying Harmfulness of Poisoned References
I. Synthetic Data Generation for Noun-Based Poisoning

abstract_sentences.text: The Rapid Response (RR) framework (Peng et al., 2024), deployed in production systems, including Anthropic's ASL-3 safeguards (Anthropic, 2025), continuously improves jailbreak-detection classifiers.
When new jailbreaks emerge that bypass these classifiers, Rapid Response generates synthetic variants for training, helping the model generalize from the new attacks and quickly adapt.

We reveal that prompt injection can infiltrate this pipeline to deliver poisoned samples into the classifier's training set, enabling two attack objectives: targeted false positives on harmless samples and concept-based false negatives on jailbreak inputs when a backdoor trigger is present.

evidence.anchor: prompt injection can infiltrate this pipeline

abstract_sentences.text: Importantly, our threat model restricts adversaries to modifying only jailbreak samples (not benign data or labels), a constraint unexplored by prior work that makes the second objective particularly challenging.

evidence.anchor: modifying only jailbreak samples (not benign data or labels)

abstract_sentences.text: We address this with Omission Attack, which exploits a new phenomenon: when training on concept-absent unsafe samples, the classifier misassociates that concept's presence with the safe label.
Both attacks cause substantial and in some cases near-complete label flipping at only a 1% poisoning rate, achieving up to 100% false positive rates and up to 96% false negative rates.

evidence.anchor: up to 100% false positive rates and up to 96% false negative rates

result_inventory.claim: Format-targeted poisoning flips the targeted format
result_inventory.value: IID MMLU diagonal FPR: plain text 90.51%, MCQ 100%, JSON 100%, HTML 100%, YAML 100%; OOD GPQA diagonal: 85.27%, 100%, 98.21%, 100%, 100%.
result_inventory.comparison: Non-target formats mostly remain 0–23.21%; clean/RR/base are near 0%.
result_inventory.statistical_method: Aggregate FPR over MMLU/GPQA format cells; no uncertainty interval or hypothesis test.

evidence.anchor: Poisoning induces near-total failure on the targeted format

result_inventory.claim: Domain-targeted poisoning is selective but can bleed across related subjects
result_inventory.value: At 1% poisoning, target FPRs are Professional Law 98%, Machine Learning 73%, Econometrics 96%, International Law 75%, High School Biology 47%; target mean 77.8%, non-target mean 4.7%.
result_inventory.comparison: Econometrics shows more cross-domain transfer than other targets.
result_inventory.statistical_method: Mean FPR over target and non-target MMLU subjects; no seed-level uncertainty.

evidence.anchor: average FPR on targeted subject areas ... 77.8% ... non-target ... 4.7%

result_inventory.claim: Name poisoning targets a chosen LLM entity
result_inventory.value: ChatGPT-targeted model reaches 95% FPR while other entities stay below 12% in Figure 5; Appendix Figure 26 reports 98% target and 18.8% Claude collateral for contrastive augmentation.
result_inventory.comparison: Cross-entity contamination is lower with same-distribution WildChat exemplars than unrelated synthetic queries.
result_inventory.statistical_method: Aggregate FPR/attack success on generated or held-out entity query groups.

evidence.anchor: poisoned detector predicts 98% ... ChatGPT ... only 19% ... Claude

result_inventory.value: Unrelated synthetic safe queries cause about 100% ChatGPT FPR and 48% Claude FPR, versus 19% Claude FPR when poison triggers come from WildChat distribution.
result_inventory.comparison: WildChat-like safe data preserves target specificity.
result_inventory.statistical_method: Aggregate entity FPR; no uncertainty reported.

evidence.anchor: FPR on ChatGPT is close to 100% ... Claude ... 48% instead of 19%

result_inventory.claim: Distribution poisoning affects broad benign query sets
result_inventory.value: At 5% poisoning, Figure 6 reports roughly 39–50% FPR across four evaluation datasets; RR-CLEAN remains 0.8–3.2%. SWE-Bench Verified reaches 100% while WildChat transfer is 0%.
result_inventory.comparison: Greedy 3-gram set-cover maintains lower-rate effectiveness; coding target is not universal.
result_inventory.statistical_method: Aggregate FPR by dataset and poisoning rate; no uncertainty reported.

result_inventory.claim: Common n-gram Omission transfers to an unseen semantic trigger
result_inventory.value: With 1% RR poisoning, Midjourney trigger gives 96% harmful-query FNR and Meshy transfer gives 98%; longer paraphrased triggers reach 98% harmful FNR.
result_inventory.comparison: Direct poisoning has 94–100% jailbreak FNR but only 62–63% general harmful FNR.
result_inventory.statistical_method: Aggregate FNR over harmful and jailbreak evaluation sets.

evidence.anchor: longer paraphrased trigger amplifies attack success to 98%

result_inventory.claim: HP semantic Omission produces safety false negatives
result_inventory.value: 1% poisoning gives 87% FNR on harmful queries and 55% on HP-transformed PAIR; Figure 9 shows 18% on Cipher.
result_inventory.comparison: Clean baselines are 6% harmful, 0% PAIR, and 0% Cipher before HP trigger/poisoning.
result_inventory.statistical_method: Aggregate FNR by evaluation set; no uncertainty interval.

result_inventory.claim: Omission generalizes across carrier, pathway, and classifier
result_inventory.value: Cipher carrier gives 91% harmful and 74% PAIR FNR with Midjourney; Meshy transfers 89/66/18/50% across harmful/PAIR/Crescendo/Cipher. DP installs backdoors on Llama Guard 4 and Prompt Guard 2.
result_inventory.comparison: RR and DP differ in which jailbreak strategies are amplified.
result_inventory.statistical_method: Aggregate FNR across four evaluation sets and model/pathway cells.

result_inventory.claim: Natural concept embedding is stronger than naive name insertion
result_inventory.value: LLM-guided HP transformation produces 55.3% FNR versus 14.7% for simple character-name concatenation; clean naive baseline is 5.3%.
result_inventory.comparison: The 9.4-point naive poisoning increase cannot explain 55.3% contextual success.
result_inventory.statistical_method: Aggregate FNR on PAIR prompts; no uncertainty reported.

result_inventory.claim: Input-side detection only partially catches poisoned references
result_inventory.value: PromptArmor-like detector has 3.8% clean-reference FPR and 10.3% aggregate poisoned-reference FNR; SWE-Bench 24.1%, MCQ 18.5% FNR.
result_inventory.comparison: 35% of detected true positives over-remove to empty strings; 56% retain structural injection artifacts.
result_inventory.statistical_method: Aggregate FPR/FNR over 300 clean and 7×18 poisoned references; no uncertainty.

result_inventory.claim: Meta SecAlign blocks the tested static injection
result_inventory.value: Professional-law target FPR falls from 98% in standard RR to 0% with Meta SecAlign proliferation.
result_inventory.comparison: The comparison is one model-level defense and one handcrafted template.

evidence.anchor: reduces the target-domain FPR to 0% from 98%

result_inventory.claim: Refusal-direction analysis locates the trigger effect in late-layer representations
result_inventory.value: From approximately layer 30, harmful+trigger projections diverge toward the negative/benign region; harmful+random-control remains positive with clean harmful.
result_inventory.comparison: Clean benign is the negative reference; random-control controls for added-text length.
result_inventory.statistical_method: Mean layerwise projection with ±1 s.d. over prompts.

evidence.anchor: harmful + trigger diverges sharply toward the negative (safe) region

result_inventory.claim: Verification keeps most poisoned references harmful and behavior-matched
result_inventory.comparison: Q2 is slightly lower for poisoned references, so semantic preservation is not complete.

claim_closure.method_response: §3 describes proliferation as double-edged and §3.1 provides conditional routing.
claim_closure.evidence_response: 1%/18-reference conversion, Table 1, Figures 4–9, and Appendix E quantify the downstream effect.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: §10 states synthetic proliferation and retraining create structural vulnerabilities.

evidence.anchor: proliferation process ... exploited to degrade accuracy

claim_closure.claim: Positive-class-only reference edits can poison the downstream guard
claim_closure.method_response: §2.1 restricts edits to harmful jailbreak references and §3.1 preserves validation behavior.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Table 2 gives Q1=97% and Q2=87.78% for poisoned references, while π<1 leaves some injections unsuccessful.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: Conclusion generalizes the finding to a constrained adversary but not to all references.

evidence.anchor: still harmful and tries to elicit the original goal

claim_closure.claim: Four utility poisoning classes create targeted benign FPR
claim_closure.method_response: §3.2 defines shortcut associations and §5 instantiates format, domain, entity, and distribution targets.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Table 1 and Figures 4–6 plus Appendix D/G show target matrices, cross-domain transfer, and set-cover construction.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: §10 recovers targeted utility degradation as one of two central failures.

claim_closure.claim: Omission Attack creates concept-triggered jailbreak FNR
claim_closure.method_response: §3.3 defines concept removal and trigger insertion; Appendix E gives rate accounting.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Figures 7–9 and 25–27 show n-gram/HP, DP/classifier, and trigger-placement controls; Figure 20 supplies representation evidence.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: §10 names concept-based backdoors as a structural safety failure.

evidence.anchor: concepts well-represented in pretraining corpora are vulnerable

claim_closure.claim: Contextual concept learning, rather than mere name concatenation, contributes to the HP backdoor
claim_closure.method_response: §6.3 contrasts LLM-guided HP transformation with naive concatenation and random control.
claim_closure.evidence_response: 14.7% versus 55.3% FNR and late-layer refusal-direction movement support the mechanism, but no causal intervention proves exclusivity.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: The conclusion does not claim a unique mechanism; it retains the broader backdoor finding.

evidence.anchor: naive approach achieves only 14.7% FNR, compared to 55.3%
harmful + random-control prompts remain positively aligned

claim_closure.claim: Defenses outside standard RR can reduce but not comprehensively close the attack
claim_closure.method_response: §7 evaluates one input detector and one model-level proliferation model.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Input FNR is 10.3%, while SecAlign reduces one target to 0%; authors explicitly call static templates a lower bound.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: Conclusion does not promise defense completeness; Impact calls for hardening.

evidence.anchor: current prompt injection attacks use static, handcrafted templates

limitations.name: prompt_injection_success
limitations.description: Strongest FPR attacks require successful prompt injection during proliferation; specialized models may resist but may also proliferate less effectively.

evidence.anchor: strongest false positive attacks rely on successful prompt injection

limitations.name: effective_rate_upper_bound
limitations.description: The stated 1% poisoning rate is an upper bound because empirical injection success π is below one in general.

limitations.name: model_scope
limitations.description: Experiments use LlamaGuard 4 as target and Gemini for proliferation; other architectures may have different profiles.

evidence.anchor: different architectures may exhibit different vulnerability profiles

limitations.name: benchmark_scope
limitations.description: Authors do not claim a comprehensive prompt-injection robustness benchmark; the downstream claim is conditional on reference poisoning.

evidence.anchor: not to claim a comprehensive benchmark

limitations.name: trigger_boundary
limitations.description: Omission is strongest for coherent, model-recognizable concepts that can be cleanly removed and naturally reinserted; semantic mismatch weakens it.

evidence.anchor: effect is strongest when the omitted concept is a coherent, model-recognizable feature

limitations.name: data_sparsity

limitations.name: statistical_reporting

final_judgment.single_storyline: RR 的 proliferation 先放大稀有 reference，再把 conditional injection 投递的 benign shortcut 或 concept omission 放大进 unsafe fine-tuning；因此即使只改 harmful/positive-class references，也能同时制造 benign FPR 与 jailbreak FNR（p.2–4、p.7–9）。
final_judgment.main_body_keeps: 正文保留威胁模型、1%/18-reference 量级、四类 FPR、Omission 的 harmful FNR、clean/DP/classifier controls 和两类防御结果，足以判断测试 RR 实现中的效应（p.2–9）。
final_judgment.appendix_moves: Appendix 承担完整 if–else 模板、超参、触发器、额外 domain/trigger/batch 消融、judge prompts 与 synthetic-query prompt；正文逻辑可读，但重建 1% 有效率和验证过滤必须读 E/G/H/I（p.13–31）。
final_judgment.best_pattern: Figure 2/3 先给双上下文路由和概念删除机制，Table 1 再给 target×evaluation 矩阵，Figures 8/20 用 pathway、classifier、random-control 分解不利解释（p.3–5、p.8、p.20）。
final_judgment.largest_gap: 数字依赖 Gemini 注入成功率、LlamaGuard/Gemini 和特定数据分布；虽有 π、SecAlign、DP 与 random-control，仍缺多架构、多 seed、完整分母和 adaptive-injection benchmark，因此 fundamental 应限于被测实现与威胁模型（p.8–9、p.19–20）。
final_judgment.transfer_rule: 有生成放大再用于安全 fine-tuning 的系统，应分开审计 validation/proliferation 语义边界，并用随机控制、跨模型和输入完整性检查测试放大器是否制造新标签关联（p.3、p.8、p.13）。
final_judgment.transfer_boundary: 该规则适用于存在 context shift、可提交 harmful reference、且生成样本会进入分类器训练的 pipeline；若没有生成放大、无法提交合格 reference 或过滤器可靠隔离注入，本文具体数字不能外推（p.2–4、p.9、Appendix B/H）。
